messages:
maya: FYI found a weird one in the sampled request logsan image attachment had EXIF name fields with a US phone number. not raw body, but still PII in metadata.
ops-bot: alert: sampled-pii-detected (route=/v1/generate) count=3 in 10m :rotating_light:
jordan: whoa. are we currently stripping EXIF on upload or just passing through?
maya: historically we only scrub text fields and attachments blobs are treated as opaque. EXIF was never sanitized.
anita: hmm that makes sense. attachments are big pain. we should avoid storing raw attachments in telemetry. options: strip EXIF on ingest, store checksum only, or pseudonymize EXIF fields.
devx: console/UX angle 7 ops need a quick way to quarantinesamples so they stop showing in admin viewers but are still available for forensics. maybe a quarantine state that replaces payload with a placeholder + hashed fingerprint.
jordan: i like quarantine + fingerprint. also we need metrics visible: `attachments.exif.pii_hits`, `attachments.quarantine.count`, `attachments.quarantine.size_bytes`.
maya: on the canary we accidentally enabled `x-dev-inspect: true` header which let the collector keep attachments. we should make headers that enable inspection require explicit RBAC and not allowed in canaries.
anita: agreed. policy proposal: header-based debug allowed only for dev tenants, blocked for prod/canary routes. enforce in ingress proxy.
devx: UX: add an action on the sample row: "Quarantine -> Scrub EXIF" that runs a server-side job to remove EXIF and replace with pseudonym token. show who clicked it and timestamp. audit trail mandatory.
jordan: implementation: we can run a lambda that rewrites object in storage: replace S3 object with exif-stripped version, store fingerprint record: `sha256(image)+route+ts`. sample table only keeps fingerprint and sanitized metadata.
maya: regex/numeric detector we used for text won't catch phone numbers hidden in EXIF tags. propose we add a small heuristic: parse EXIF text fields and run the same detectors (ssn/phone/email). quick example: `exif_text -> re.search(r"\b\d{3}[-.]?\d{3}[-.]?\d{4}\b")`.
anita: don't forget international numbers. maybe run libphonenumber for accuracy. but that increases CPU cost on ingest; we should sample-check with cost cap.
jordan: telemetry quota note: parsing EXIF for every image is expensive. let's run full EXIF PII detection only on sampled telemetry (1 in 100) and run a lightweight strip for all uploads on dedicated customers who enable attachment-scrub.
devx: rollout plan: 1) enable quarantine action + fingerprint storage (ops-only) behind feature flag; 2) enable EXIF parse on sampled telemetry; 3) add per-tenant setting `attachments.exif_scrub=on|off|sampled`; 4) after canary, ship console button for scrubbing and audit modal.
maya: runbook addendum: if attachments.exif.pii_hits > 5/min for a route, auto-quarantine newest 100 samples and escalate to security. ops-bot can trigger that.
ops-bot: rule added: auto-quarantine on threshold for route /v1/generate (threshold=5/min) :white_check_mark:
anita: KMS/consent: for pseudonymization tokens use tenant-scoped HMAC key from KMS, rotate monthly. store only truncated hex (first 12 chars) as token to reduce ability to brute-force.
jordan: retention: quarantined samples should have a separate TTL (90 days) and must be hard-deleted on a verified DSAR. normal sampled telemetry stays at 30 days. document in privacy runbook.
devx: small config snippet for the feature flag API:
```json
{ "route": "/v1/generate", "feature": "attachments.quarantine", "state": "on", "allowed_roles": ["ops", "sec"] }
```
maya: tests: unit test to assert EXIF strip runs when feature on and header `x-dev-inspect` is absent. also integration that ensures quarantine replaces stored blob with placeholder and keeps fingerprint.
anita: compliance question: do we need tenant consent toggle to allow storing fingerprint? i think fingerprint is allowed if non-reversible, but legal should confirm. add to RFC.
jordan: filing short RFC now: attachments-exif-quarantine + metrics + console flows. target review in 48h.
devx: I'll wire the console action and audit modal prototype this week. ops-bot: posting event redwood.audit:attachments.quarantine.policy.created user=devx ts=5619876576
maya: thanks all. please keep canary headers strict. follow up on RFC + add a dashboard panel for `attachments.exif.pii_hits` and `attachments.quarantine.rate`. closing when RFC merged. :thumbsup:"
